cells.tense: Present — you're here, with the pen.
cells.verb: letting what's finished end so what's next has room
cells.place: right at the threshold where the new thing is coming in
cells.ask: Let what you take in be as free as what you let go — notice the exchange, don't tally it — and what's ending stays honored while what's arriving stays trusted.
cells.core:
You can feel when something is done, and you let it be done. Not tearing it down, not dragging it out — the thing that was finishes, and you turn to what's coming through the door with your hands open. That timing is yours; you're reading what's arriving and meeting it.

What this frees up is a kind of evenness. What you release and what you receive can start to balance each other without you keeping score. Let the trade run loose — give what's finished its ending, take what's new without checking the ledger — and the endings keep their dignity while the next thing keeps your trust.
cells.sheetLine: You let what's done be done, and you trust what's coming in.

cells.tense: Future — bracing for a version of this that hasn't happened yet.
cells.verb: ending things before they've had a chance to live
cells.place: at the door, where almost anything new looks like a threat on its way in
cells.ask: Stay with one thing — or one person — long enough to actually feel what it is before you decide it's over, keeping yourself in the room while you do; what comes back is ending only what truly needs to end, and trusting the rest to arrive.
cells.core:
You're clearing out faster than anything can take root. Something new comes through the door and part of you is already writing its ending, calling it freedom — but the speed is fear wearing freedom's clothes. Nothing gets far enough to become anything, so nothing can disappoint you, and nothing can feed you either.

The way back isn't to grip harder. It's to stay in contact. Let one thing be what it is for a while, feel it from the inside instead of from the exit, without losing yourself in it. Felt that way, the real endings announce themselves and the false ones quiet down — and what's arriving gets to be met instead of pre-emptively cleared.
cells.sheetLine: You're ending things before they've lived, and calling it freedom.

cells.tense: Past — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: holding on to what has already finished
cells.place: at the threshold, with your back to what's trying to come in
cells.ask: Put your energy toward one thing you genuinely want — a step toward, not a step away from what you're holding — and the ending takes care of itself, honored instead of forced, with what's new finally able to enter.
cells.core:
Something is over and you're still keeping it company. You'd call it loyalty, and maybe part of it is, but the thing itself is done and you're the only one still showing up for it. Meanwhile what's new is at the door and you haven't turned around.

Don't try to pry your hands off. That rarely works, and it doesn't need to. Instead, find the one thing you actually want right now — want from the gut, not from obligation — and move toward it, even a little. Real motion in the direction of something alive is what loosens the grip on what isn't. The ending happens on its own then, with your respect rather than your resistance, and what's arriving gets to arrive.
cells.sheetLine: You're staying loyal to something that's already over.

cells.tense: Disowned present — you're already in the middle of this, pen down.
cells.verb: letting something finish without knowing it's finishing
cells.place: at the door, with something already leaving as something else comes in
cells.ask: Lay it out plainly — what's actually here now and what isn't anymore, just the inventory, no story — and the ending comes into view where you can honor it, and what's entering becomes something you can trust.
cells.core:
Something in you is ending, and you haven't noticed. You'd say things feel off, unsettled, a little hollow, and you might blame the weather or the week — but a thing that was you is quietly finishing, and something else is already coming through the door to take its place. The change is underway. The knowing isn't.

The simplest help is to make it legible. Put down, in plain words, what's actually present in your life right now and what has gone quiet or missing — no explanations, just the shape of it. Clear structure like that doesn't force anything; it lets you see what's already true. Seen, the ending can be honored instead of just suffered, and what's arriving stops being a vague disturbance and becomes something you can meet.
cells.sheetLine: Something in you is ending. You haven't noticed yet.
